title: प्रधानमन्त्रीले चाल्ने कदममा रास्वपाको पूर्ण समर्थन रहन्छ : प्रवक्ता खरेल
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा)का प्रवक्ता जगदीश खरेलले सरकार सञ्चालनका क्रममा प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन शाहले चाल्ने कदममा पार्टीको पूर्ण समर्थन रहने बताएका छन् । विमानस्थलमा सांसदहरूको बिदाइका क्रममा सञ्चारकर्मीसँग कुरा गर्दै प्रवक्ता खरेलले सरकारका आन्तरिक कामकारबाहीमा पार्टीले हस्तक्षेप गर्न नचाहेको स्पष्ट पारेका हुन् । सरकारअन्तर्गतका निकाय तथा व्यक्तिहरूका विषयमा पार्टीले अत्यधिक चासो राख्दा हस्तक्षेप गरेको अर्थ लाग्न सक्ने भन्दै उनले सम्बन्धित विषयमा निर्णय गर्ने जिम्मेवारी प्रधानमन्त्रीकै भएको बताए । उनले भने, ‘प्रधानमन्त्रीज्यूले केही कुरा गलत भइरहेको छ र अब एक्सन लिनुपर्छ भन्ने महसुस गर्नुभयो भने उहाँले चाल्ने कदममा पार्टीको सम्पूर्ण समर्थन रहन्छ ।’ गृहमन्त्री, प्रधानमन्त्रीका सल्लाहकार तथा सरकारका अन्य व्यक्तिहरूका विषयमा सार्वजनिक रूपमा उठिरहेका प्रश्नहरू पार्टीको औपचारिक छलफलमा प्रवेश नगरेको पनि उनले बताए । ती विषयमा प्रधानमन्त्रीले के सोचिरहनुभएको छ र सरकारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने विषयमा पार्टीले प्रतीक्षा गरिरहेको उनले बताए । सरकारलाई स्वतन्त्र रूपमा काम गर्न दिनुपर्ने पार्टीको मान्यता रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै खरेलले सभापति, महामन्त्रीसहित पार्टीको नेतृत्व र सम्पूर्ण टोली सरकार सञ्चालनमा कुनै अवरोध वा हस्तक्षेपको महसुस नहोस् भन्नेमा सचेत रहेको बताए । त्यस्तै, नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक (आईजीपी) लाई हटाउने वा राख्ने विषयमा पार्टीले सरकारलाई कुनै निर्देशन नदिएको उनले स्पष्ट पारे । आईजीपीलाई हटाऊ वा राख भनेर पार्टीले निर्देशन नदिएको भन्दै उनले यो सरकारको विवेक र निर्णयको विषय भएको बताए । उक्त विषय अदालतसम्म पुगेको र कतिपय प्रक्रिया अघि बढिरहेको अवस्थामा सरकारले आवश्यकताअनुसार थप स्पष्ट पार्दै जाने उनले उल्लेख गरे । यसैबीच, रास्वपाको २० सदस्यीय प्रतिनिधिमण्डल महामन्त्री विपिनकुमार आचार्यको नेतृत्वमा मित्रराष्ट्र चीन भ्रमणमा जान लागेको प्रवक्ता खरेलले जानकारी दिए । चीनको सत्तारुढ दलले रास्वपालाई निमन्त्रणा गरेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले यो भ्रमण दुई देशका सत्तारुढ दलबीचको निमन्त्रणाअनुसार हुन लागेको बताए । Kathmandu. Jagdish Kharel, spokesperson of the National Independent Party (NIP), has said that the party will have full support for the steps taken by Prime Minister Balen Shah during the government's tenure. Speaking to media persons during the farewell of the lawmakers at the airport, Spokesperson Kharel made it clear that the party does not want to interfere in the internal affairs of the government. Stating that the party's excessive interest in the affairs of government bodies and individuals could be interpreted as interference, he said that the responsibility to make decisions on related matters lies with the Prime Minister. He said, "If the Prime Minister feels that something is wrong and action needs to be taken now, the party will have full support in the steps he takes." He also said that the questions being raised publicly regarding the Home Minister, the Prime Minister's advisors and other government officials have not entered the party's formal discussions. He said that the party is waiting to hear what the Prime Minister is thinking and what the government is doing on these issues. Stating that the party believes that the government should be allowed to function independently, Kharel said that the party leadership, including the president, general secretary, and the entire team are aware that there is no sense of obstruction or interference in the operation of the government. Similarly, he clarified that the party has not given any instructions to the government regarding the removal or retention of the Inspector General of Nepal Police (IGP). Stating that the party has not given any instructions to remove or retain the IGP, he said that it is a matter of the government's discretion and decision. He mentioned that the matter has reached the court and some processes are underway, and the government will provide further clarification as needed. Meanwhile, a 20-member delegation of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) led by General Secretary Bipin Kumar Acharya is set to visit friendly country China, Spokesperson Kharel informed. Stating that the ruling party of China has invited the RSS, he said that the visit is being held as per the invitation between the ruling parties of the two countries.

Jagdish Kharel, spokesperson of the National Independent Party (NIP), has said that the party will have full support for the steps taken by Prime Minister Balen Shah during the government's tenure. Speaking to media persons during the farewell of the lawmakers at the airport, Spokesperson Kharel made it clear that the party does not want to interfere in the internal affairs of the government. Stating that the party's excessive interest in the affairs of government bodies and individuals could be interpreted as interference, he said that the responsibility to make decisions on related matters lies with the Prime Minister. He said, "If the Prime Minister feels that something is wrong and action needs to be taken now, the party will have full support in the steps he takes." He also said that the questions being raised publicly regarding the Home Minister, the Prime Minister's advisors and other government officials have not entered the party's formal discussions. He said that the party is waiting to hear what the Prime Minister is thinking and what the government is doing on these issues. Stating that the party believes that the government should be allowed to function independently, Kharel said that the party leadership, including the president, general secretary, and the entire team are aware that there is no sense of obstruction or interference in the operation of the government. Similarly, he clarified that the party has not given any instructions to the government regarding the removal or retention of the Inspector General of Nepal Police (IGP). Stating that the party has not given any instructions to remove or retain the IGP, he said that it is a matter of the government's discretion and decision. He mentioned that the matter has reached the court and some processes are underway, and the government will provide further clarification as needed. Meanwhile, a 20-member delegation of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) led by General Secretary Bipin Kumar Acharya is set to visit friendly country China, Spokesperson Kharel informed. Stating that the ruling party of China has invited the RSS, he said that the visit is being held as per the invitation between the ruling parties of the two countries.

आईजीपीलाई हटाऊ वा राख भनेर पार्टीले निर्देशन नदिएको भन्दै उनले यो सरकारको विवेक र निर्णयको विषय भएको बताए । उक्त विषय अदालतसम्म पुगेको र कतिपय प्रक्रिया अघि बढिरहेको अवस्थामा सरकारले आवश्यकताअनुसार थप स्पष्ट पार्दै जाने उनले उल्लेख गरे ।

यसैबीच, रास्वपाको २० सदस्यीय प्रतिनिधिमण्डल महामन्त्री विपिनकुमार आचार्यको नेतृत्वमा मित्रराष्ट्र चीन भ्रमणमा जान लागेको प्रवक्ता खरेलले जानकारी दिए । चीनको सत्तारुढ दलले रास्वपालाई निमन्त्रणा गरेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले यो भ्रमण दुई देशका सत्तारुढ दलबीचको निमन्त्रणाअनुसार हुन लागेको बताए ।

Kathmandu. Jagdish Kharel, spokesperson of the National Independent Party (NIP), has said that the party will have full support for the steps taken by Prime Minister Balen Shah during the government's tenure. Speaking to media persons during the farewell of the lawmakers at the airport, Spokesperson Kharel made it clear that the party does not want to interfere in the internal affairs of the government. Stating that the party's excessive interest in the affairs of government bodies and individuals could be interpreted as interference, he said that the responsibility to make decisions on related matters lies with the Prime Minister. He said, "If the Prime Minister feels that something is wrong and action needs to be taken now, the party will have full support in the steps he takes." He also said that the questions being raised publicly regarding the Home Minister, the Prime Minister's advisors and other government officials have not entered the party's formal discussions. He said that the party is waiting to hear what the Prime Minister is thinking and what the government is doing on these issues. Stating that the party believes that the government should be allowed to function independently, Kharel said that the party leadership, including the president, general secretary, and the entire team are aware that there is no sense of obstruction or interference in the operation of the government. Similarly, he clarified that the party has not given any instructions to the government regarding the removal or retention of the Inspector General of Nepal Police (IGP). Stating that the party has not given any instructions to remove or retain the IGP, he said that it is a matter of the government's discretion and decision. He mentioned that the matter has reached the court and some processes are underway, and the government will provide further clarification as needed. Meanwhile, a 20-member delegation of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) led by General Secretary Bipin Kumar Acharya is set to visit friendly country China, Spokesperson Kharel informed. Stating that the ruling party of China has invited the RSS, he said that the visit is being held as per the invitation between the ruling parties of the two countries.
